question.text: If the image of the point $(4,4,3)$ in the line $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-2}{1}=\frac{z-1}{3}$ is $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is equal to

solution.text: Let coordinate of $R=(2 r+1, r+2,3 r+1)$ $\because \quad P R$ is perpendicular to given line. $\therefore(2 r-3) \cdot 2+(r-2) \cdot 1+(3 r-2) \cdot 3=0$ $\therefore r=1$ $\therefore$ Coordinate of $R=(3,3,4)$ $\therefore \quad(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)=(2,2,5)$ $\therefore \alpha+\beta+\gamma=9$
